summary:
AstraMed is an AI-powered health monitoring platform designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. Spaceflight can affect cardiovascular health, bone and muscle strength, immunity, sleep patterns and mental well-being. Monitoring these changes is essential for keeping astronauts healthy and mission-ready.

AstraMed brings health indicators together in one platform. It is designed to collect information from wearable devices, daily health logs, exercise records and medical inputs. Its AI analysis examines health trends, learns individual patterns and identifies unusual changes that may require attention. The platform presents health trends, alerts and understandable insights through an astronaut dashboard.

By combining personalised monitoring with anomaly detection, AstroHealth aims to help astronauts better understand their health and support more informed decisions during missions to the International Space Station, the Moon and Mars.
details:
Project Overview

AstraMed is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support health awareness during long-duration space missions. It focuses on the health challenges astronauts may experience in space, including cardiovascular changes, bone and muscle loss, weakened immunity, sleep disturbances and mental stress.

Data Sources and Data Processing

AstraMed uses a combination of publicly available physiological datasets and NASA space-life-science resources to support its development and evaluation.

  • NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR/ALSDA): Provides spaceflight and space-relevant life-science research data that helps inform the project's astronaut-health context.
  • PhysioNet BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset: Provides physiological signals and measurements, including ECG, PPG, heart rate, respiratory rate and SpO₂, for developing and testing physiological-data processing and anomaly-detection workflows.
  • PhysioNet MIMIC-III Clinical Database: Provides de-identified clinical information and vital-sign records for additional research and validation, subject to its credentialed-access requirements.

These sources have different populations and collection environments. Clinical datasets are used as supporting physiological references and are not treated as direct representations of astronaut health. Spaceflight-specific findings are interpreted in the context of NASA research.

The platform aims to combine physiological trends, individual baselines and mission-related context to generate understandable health insights. Its outputs are intended for experimental decision support, not medical diagnosis.

How It Works

https://youtu.be/wy9KcpDDcCY

The proposed system collects health information from four sources:

  • Wearable devices, including heart rate, SpO₂ and activity measurements.
  • Daily health logs, including sleep and stress information.
  • Exercise records to monitor physical activity and workload.
  • Periodic medical assessments and inputs.

The backend processes the collected information and stores health records. An AI analysis engine examines trends, learns individual health patterns, identifies unusual deviations and generates health alerts and insights.

The astronaut dashboard is designed to display health measurements, historical trends, alerts, explanations and personalised recommendations.

Key Features and Innovation

  1. Vital Sign Monitoring: Tracks important physiological indicators such as heart rate, heart rate variability, SpO₂ and blood pressure.
  2. Activity and Muscle Health: Uses exercise and activity information to understand physical workload.
  3. Sleep and Recovery Analysis: Examines sleep duration, quality and patterns.
  4. Immune and Wellness Tracking: Supports monitoring of indicators related to immune health and general well-being.
  5. Mental Well-being Support: Includes periodic check-ins and behavioural information.
  6. AI Insights and Alerts: Identifies unusual patterns and presents understandable health insights.

The main innovation is bringing multiple health dimensions together and analysing changes in relation to an astronaut's individual patterns, rather than treating every measurement independently.

Technologies and Tools

  • Frontend: React with Vite
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • Database: PostgreSQL
  • AI/ML: Anomaly detection and health-pattern analysis
  • Deployment: Docker

Intended Impact

AstraMed aims to improve astronaut health awareness, support the identification of unusual health patterns and provide useful information for health-related decisions during long-duration missions. Its future scope includes supporting missions to the Moon and Mars, where access to immediate medical assistance may be limited.

Limitations

AstraMed is a prototype concept for health monitoring and decision support. Its alerts and insights are not medical diagnoses, and its effectiveness would require validation using appropriate real-world data and medical expertise.
